relationships.subject: disulfide HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: Intra-articular disulfide HMGB1 evoked mechanical hypersensitivity in male and female C57BL/6

relationships.subject: all-thiol HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: all-thiol HMGB1 did not evoke mechanical hypersensitivity in either male or female mice after intra-articular injection

relationships.subject: 2G7
relationships.evidence_quote: it significantly reversed CAIA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity at 3, 75, and 120 hours postinjection in male but not in female mice

relationships.subject: disulfide HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: We found a significant increase of TNF, IL-6, and CXCL1 levels in culture supernatant of macrophages derived from male mice after stimulation with disulfide HMGB1

relationships.subject: minocycline
relationships.evidence_quote: which was prevented when minocycline at both 30 and 100 μg was coadministered with HMGB1 in male mice

relationships.subject: TLR4 on nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: TLR4 depletion in sensory neurons protected both male and female mice from developing disulfide HMGB1-induced hypersensitivity

relationships.subject: TLR4 on myeloid cells
relationships.evidence_quote: the overall consequence of TLR4 ablation in myeloid cells yields a statistically significant reduction of HMGB1-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in male but not female mice

relationships.subject: disulfide HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: the disulfide form, which acts on TLR4 and induces cytokine production

relationships.subject: all-thiol HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: released in the reduced all-thiol form, binds to receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE)

key_findings: Disulfide but not all-thiol HMGB1 induces joint pain in both sexes; blocking peripheral HMGB1 reverses CAIA hypersensitivity only in males
Macrophage/myeloid TLR4 contributes more in males, whereas nociceptor TLR4 mediates HMGB1 pain in both sexes
